methods.label: Match factors and signs
methods.sourceMethod: Express each reversed difference as a negative matching factor, then cancel the nonzero factors.

annotationRationale: The question tests multiplication and reduction of rational expressions, with sign reversal exposing the factors to cancel. The stated restrictions justify every cancellation.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is correct; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Every denominator is nonzero under the stated restrictions. Its product is the negative of the numerator product, so the expression is always -1, matching A. There is no statement, key, or figure contradiction.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The supplied sign-pairing solutions use the same essential idea. Numerical substitution alone would not justify the value for every permitted triple, so no additional method is required.
review.annotationCheck: cnm_160 appropriately identifies multiplication and reduction of rational expressions. The restrictions are correctly used to justify cancellation. The broader US link is limited to its applicable component below.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is correct; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The three reversed differences each contribute a factor of -1. Their product is (-1)^3 = -1. All matched factors are nonzero, so cancellation yields 1/(-1)^3 = -1.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: LIVE supports this factor-and-sign argument. The candidate adds its own structural motivation and explicit domain justification; the shared equations are mathematically necessary. source-informed-original accurately identifies the third-party basis.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation makes the matching pattern visible before calculating, shows all three sign reversals, and explains exactly why cancellation is permitted.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_160 directly describes multiplying rational expressions and reducing the resulting product. No unsupported node is included.
